headline: Awarded $1,673,371 Edgewood Pre-K Academy demolition contract; approved $4,250,000 outdoor recreation grant; rejected $175,000 offer for 81 Church Avenue.
summary: The council approved a $1,673,371 demolition contract for the Edgewood Pre-K Academy renovation and a $4,250,000 grant application for outdoor recreation. It rejected a $175,000 offer for 81 Church Avenue and introduced amendments to Appendix D, Flood Damage Prevention, with a public hearing set for September 1, 2026. It also adopted a higher $120 citation fine, and council members discussed license plate reader cameras without a vote.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 14, 2026 City Council meeting, unanimously.
Placed the July 2026 New Hire Report on file, unanimously.
Approved $151,894.72 in tax refunds, unanimously.
Placed on file the Planning Commission positive referral for the sale of Witches Rock Road, Map 8, Lot 6+7+8, unanimously.
Placed on file the Planning Commission positive referral for the sale of Kilmartin Avenue, Map 8, Lot 88, unanimously.
Accepted $328,029 in funding from Shine Early Learning, unanimously.
Approved submission of a CT DECD Municipal Brownfield Remediation Grant application for Cambridge Park Limited Partnership, unanimously, and referred the matter to the Board of Finance.
Approved an amendment to the Fiducient Advisors agreement for the deferred compensation program, unanimously, and referred it to the Board of Finance and Corporation Counsel.
Awarded Contract 2P26-075 for leasing of computer equipment to CCA Financial LLC, unanimously.
Approved submission of a grant application of at least $1,000 to the CT Office of the Arts Supporting Arts Grant Program, unanimously.
Introduced amendments to Appendix D, Flood Damage Prevention, and set a public hearing for Tuesday, September 1, 2026 at 4:50 p.m., unanimously.
Adopted additions to Section 23-5 raising the citation fine from $90 to $120, unanimously.
Rejected the $175,000 offer from JBS Developers, LLC for 81 Church Avenue, unanimously.
Directed the Purchasing Agent to issue a request for proposals to sell Lot 6+7+8 Witches Rock Road, with no minimum price, unanimously.
Approved creating a part-time Arts & Culture Coordinator position, unanimously.
Approved reappointing 21 members and appointing four new members to the Bristol Early Childhood Collaborative, unanimously.
Approved reappointment of John Lodovico to the Building Code of Appeals by voice vote.
Approved appointment of Jeffrey Beauchamp to the Bristol Burlington Health District Commission by voice vote.
Approved appointment of Nicholas Palmer as alternate to the Fair Rent Commission by voice vote.
Approved appointment of Dannette Rodriguez to the Board of Fire Commissioners by voice vote.
Approved reappointment of Ann Bednaz as Tax Collector by voice vote.
Approved a $4,250,000 grant application to the CT DEEP Outdoor Recreation and Legacy Partnership Program with a $2,125,000 City match, unanimously.
Awarded bid package 1.2.1 for Edgewood Pre-K Academy demolition and HAZMAT removal to American Building Wreckers for $1,673,371.00, unanimously.

405 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council was held on Wednesday, August 12, 2026 in the 
City Hall Council Chambers, 111 North Main Street at 7:00 p.m. Present: Mayor Zoppo-Sassu; 
Council Members Dickau, Hahn, Kelley, Rosengren, and Tyler.  Absent:  Council Member Seymour. 
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
   
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was 
unanimously voted:  To approve the minutes of the regular City Council meeting held on July 14, 
2026. 
   
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION  
 
 Correspondence from Mathew Biadun, 53 Buff Road –  Mr. Biadun’s letter cites examples of 
concerning situations involving the Flock camera brand.  He further urges Bristol not to allow its 
surveillance systems to aid federal agencies, and to consider other license plate reader suppliers.  
 
 Gabby Carrano, 70 Seneca Rd. – Ms. Carrano spoke about what she referred to as “the 
erosion of civil liberties and privacy rights” in regards to red light cameras, speed cameras, and 
automated license plate readers. 
 
 Shelley Mastroianni, 120 Sixth St. – Ms. Mastroianni spoke in opposition to data centers, 
stating that data centers are paving the way to a robotic world, which will in turn take away blue 
collar jobs from communities. 
 
 David Haberfeld, 110 Divinity St. – Mr. Haberfeld spoke in opposition to red light cameras 
and speeding cameras.  He feels that it is unfair to ticket the owner of the car instead of the driver and 
provided various scenarios to support his opinion. 
 
 Sarah Pagano, 52 Irving St. – Ms. Pagano stated that she has read stories of Flock cameras 
being used in other states to track people and she is concerned that it will happen in Bristol. 
 
4. ANNOUNCEMENTS  
 
Council members reported on committees, activities, and events.   
 
 Mayor Zoppo-Sassu announced that she, Chief Morello, and Council Members Kelley 
and Tyler attended a Symposium on automated license plate reader cameras.  Mayor Zoppo-
Sassu commented that there are currently 14 Flock cameras and the City is looking to move 
away from Flock and onto Axon.  Axon is the company already used for dash cameras and body 
cameras.  Any money collected from red light cameras will be segregated for traffic safety 
improvements.   
 
Chief Morello explained that data collected in Bristol is saved for 21 days and then 
automatically deleted, unless it is needed for an active police investigation.  He further stated that 
collected data would only be used within the state of Connecticut.  Chief Morello reminded 
everyone that Flock is a brand name for a license plate reader and that Bristol intends to use
406 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
Axon as the vendor for its license plate readers (LPR).  He explained that the data from the 
City’s LPRs will be locked on the cloud and his department has taken every measure possible to 
ensure the date collected is protected.  To illustrate the benefits of LPRs, Chief Morello briefly 
spoke about the numerous arrests in Bristol that resulted from data on the license plate readers.  
Council members posed clarifying questions and provided their opinions on the cameras. 
 
5.  ADOPTION OF CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
 On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Rosengren, it was 
unanimously voted:  To adopt nine items as part of the Consent Calendar.   
 
a. New Hire Report for July 2026 
 
Communication received from the Human Resources Department. 
 
 As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To place on file the New Hire Report for the month of  
July, 2026. 
 
b. Tax Refunds in the Amount of $151,894.72 
 
Request presented from Tax Collector Bednaz. 
 
As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted: To approve the Tax Refunds as follows –  
 
Motor Vehicle               $   4,418.29       
Real Estate             + 147,476.43      
                                       Total   $151,894.72  
           
c.  Positive Referral – Witches Rock Road, Map 8, Lot 6+7+8 
 
     Communication received from the Bristol Planning Commission. 
 
     As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To place on file a positive referral from the Planning 
Commission for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of Witches Rock Road, Map 8, Lot 6+7+8 to sell the 
property. 
 
d.  Positive Referral – Kilmartin Avenue, Map 8, Lot 88 
 
     Communication received from the Bristol Planning Commission. 
 
     As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To place on file a positive referral from the Planning 
Commission for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review of Kilmartin Avenue, Map 8, Lot 88 to sell the 
property.
407 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
e.   Acceptance of Funding from Shine Early Learning 
 
      Communication received from Bristol Early Childhood Collaborative Liaison Osuch. 
 
      As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To accept funding from Shine Early Learning for $328,029 to 
support the work of the Bristol Early Childhood Collaborative through June 30, 2027.   
 
f.  CT DECD Brownfields Grant Application 
 
     Communication received from Grants Administrator Leger.  
 
     As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To approve submission of an application for funds to the CT 
DECD Municipal Brownfield Remediation Grant Program as a Pass-Through Entity on behalf of the 
Cambridge Park Limited Partnership, to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all 
documents associated with the application/grant, and to refer the matter to the Board of Finance for 
any necessary action.   
 
g.  Fiducient Advisors Agreement 
 
 Communication received from Comptroller Waldron. 
 
 As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute an 
amendment to the Fiducient Advisors (Fiduciary Investment Advisors) agreement dated January 27, 
2020, to appoint Fiducient as Discretionary Investment Manager for the City's voluntary deferred 
compensation retirement program with MissionSquare and to refer this matter to the Board of 
Finance and the Corporation Counsel's office for review. 
 
h.  Contract 2P26-075 Leasing of Computer Equipment 
 
     Communication received from Purchasing Agent Haynes. 
 
     As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To award Contract 2P26-075 Leasing of Computer Equipment 
to CCA Financial LLC and to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all 
documents necessary to effectuate said contract.  
 
i. Supporting Arts Grant Program 
     
     Communication received from Grants Administrator Leger. 
 
    As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded, it was unanimously voted:  To approve the submission of a grant application in the amount 
of at least $1,000 for Operating Expenses to the CT Office of the Arts Supporting Arts Grant 
Program; to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all documents related to this 
grant, and to refer the matter to the Board of Finance for any necessary action.
408 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
6. REPORTS AND COMMITTEE REPORTS  
 
a.  Ordinance Committee 
On recommendation of the Ordinance Committee and on motion of Council Member Dickau 
and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted:  In accordance with 
Section 41(f) of the Charter of the City of Bristol, to waive the reading of the proposed 
amendments to Appendix D, Flood Damage Prevention, of the Code of Ordinances being 
introduced this date.    
 
On motion of Council Member Dickau and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was 
unanimously voted:  To introduce the following amendments to Appendix D, Flood Damage 
Prevention, of the Bristol Code of Ordinances; to set Tuesday, September 1, 2026 at 4:50 
p.m., in Meeting Room 1-1, City Hall, First Floor, 111 North Main Street, Bristol, 
Connecticut for the holding of a Public Hearing by the Ordinance Committee, and that the 
City Clerk publish notice of said Public Hearing and the proposed amendments to the Code 
of Ordinances as required by City Charter.  
 
Upon request by Council Member Hahn, Council Member Dickau provided a summary of 
reasons for the proposed changes.   
 
Refer to attached copy of Appendix D. 
Underscored text is proposed to be added.  [Bracketed] text is proposed for deletion. 
 
b.  Ordinance Committee 
On recommendation of the Ordinance Committee and on motion of Council Member Dickau 
and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted: To adopt additions to 
Chapter 23 Ordinance Enforcement by Citation Officers, Section 23-5 Penalties for Offenses, 
of the Bristol Code of Ordinances to read as follows; that the City Clerk publish said 
additions to the Code of Ordinances, and that they become effective upon the expiration of 14 
days from the date of their publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the City of 
Bristol; and to waive the reading of said ordinance. 
 
Underscored text is proposed to be added.  [Bracketed] text is proposed for deletion. 
 
Sec. 23-5. Penalties for offenses. 
 
Unless otherwise provided, any violation enforceable by citation shall be punishable by a fine of 
[ninety dollars ($90.00)] one hundred twenty dollars ($120.00). Each day a violation continues shall 
constitute a separate offense. In addition to the fines set forth in this subsection, an additional 
administrative fee of two dollars ($2.00) per ten dollars ($10.00) of the amount of the fine(s) payable 
hereunder, or any fraction thereof, shall be payable to the city by each person to whom a citation is 
issued. The initial penalty for any citation not paid or under appeal shall double after fifteen (15) 
days and triple after thirty (30) days.   (Amend. eff. 11-29-19) 
 
 c.  Real Estate Committee  
 On recommendation of the Real Estate Committee and on motion of Council Member Hahn 
 and seconded by Council Member Rosengren, it was unanimously voted:  To reject the offer 
 from JBS Developers, LLC in the amount of $175,000 in response to the City of Bristol's
409 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
 RFP 2026-059 for the sale of Surplus Property on 81 Church Avenue, Assessor's Map 43, Lot 
 22.   
 
 It was further moved to direct the Purchasing Agent to reissue another RFP (Request For 
 Proposal) placing public notices and to notify abutting property owners of the city's intention 
 to sell city-owned property known as 81 Church Avenue, Map 43, Lot 22.  The asking price 
 in the RFP shall be amended downward to $300,000. 
 
 d.  Real Estate Committee 
 On recommendation of the Real Estate Committee and on motion of Council Member 
 Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted:  To 
 direct the Purchasing Agent to issue an RFP (Request For Proposal) placing public notices 
 and to notify abutting property owners of the city’s intention to sell city-owned property 
 known as Lot 6+7+8 Witches Rock Road on Tax Assessor’s Map 8.  The Purchasing Agent 
 is not to set a minimum price as the Real Estate Committee is requesting to review all offers. 
 
 e.  Salary Committee 
 On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Rosengren, it was 
 unanimously voted to add item 6e. from the Salary Committee to the agenda. 
 
 On recommendation of the Salary Committee and on motion of Council Member Hahn 
 and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted:  To approve the 
 creation of a part-time, non-bargaining, Arts & Culture Coordinator position funded through 
 the Arts & Culture Special Revenue Fund. 
 
 Joshua Medeiros, Superintendent of Parks, Recreation, Youth & Community Services 
 provided information on the justification for the position and stated that it would have no 
 financial impact to the City General Fund. 
  
 Council members reported on other committees, activities, and events.   
    
7. OLD BUSINESS – None. 
  
8. NEW BUSINESS – None. 
 
9.  RESIGNATIONS -  None.  
   
10.  Appointments 
   
a.  The following appointments were presented: 
 
Bristol Early Childhood Collaborative 
 On motion of Council Member Hahn, and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was 
 unanimously voted:  To reappoint 21 members and appoint four new members of the Bristol 
 Early Childhood Collaborative, each with a term to expire in August 2028.  The 
 reappointments and appoints are as follows:
410 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
 Reappointments – Maegan Adams, Kaitlyn Berardinelli, Janelle Cintolo, Michelle Fangiullo, 
 Yesenia Fuentes, Cecilia Garay, Sandra Godin, Cristina Gutierrez, Michelle Herens, Donna 
 Koser, Susan Lee MD, Amber Lipscomb, Zachary Maher, Liz McGuire, Melissa Mendez, 
 Brenda Moore, Valerie Pelletier, Whitney Shufelt, Kara Singleton, Claire Strillacci, Courtney 
 Sugarman. 
 
 Appointments – Jeffrey Arduini, Bristol Parks, Recreation, Youth & Community Services; 
 Christopher Badenhop, Badenhop Consulting LLC; Yolande Lazaruz-Guerrero, New 
 Beginnings Early Learning Center; Elizabeth Rodriguez, parent representative. 
  
 Building Code of Appeals 
 John Lodovico – Reappointment – term to 8/31. 
 Confirming motion by Council Member Hahn. 
 Motion passed in voice vote. 
  
 Bristol Burlington Health District Commission 
 Jeffrey Beauchamp – Appointment – term to 7/29. 
 Replaced R. Wollenberg. 
 Confirming motion by Council Member Tyler. 
 Motion passed in voice vote. 
 
 Fair Rent Commission 
 Nicholas Palmer – Appointment as alternate, representing “Landlords” – term to 5/28. 
 Replaced C. Cohen. 
 Confirming motion by Council Member Hahn. 
 Motion passed in voice vote. 
 
 Board of Fire Commissioners 
 Dannette Rodriguez – Appointment – term to 1/28. 
 Replaced S. Moore. 
 Confirming motion by Council Member Rosengren. 
 Motion passed in voice vote. 
 
 Tax Collector 
 Ann Bednaz – Reappointment – term to 8/30. 
 Confirming motion by Council Member Tyler. 
 Motion passed in voice vote. 
 
11. GRANTS 
 
 Communication received from PRYCS Superintendent Medeiros. 
 
 On recommendation of the Salary Committee and on motion of Council Member Hahn and 
seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted:  To approve submission of a grant 
application in the amount of $4,250,000 to the CT Department of Energy and Environmental 
Protection's Outdoor Recreation and Legacy Partnership Program, with a City match of $2,125,000; 
to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all documents related to this grant, and to 
refer the matter to the Board of Finance for any necessary action.
411 
AUGUST 12, 2026 
 
 Superintendent Medeiros explained that this project is a revitalization of the Hoppers -Birge 
Pond area, including but not limited to fixing the dam, boardwalk repair, and trail restoration.  He 
further explained that the project has been in the capital improvement plan, but money has not yet 
been appropriated for it. 
 
12. CONTRACTS 
 
 a.  Bid Package 1.2.1. Demolition & HAZMAT Removal – Edgewood Pre-K Academy 
 
 Communication received from Schools Project Manager Landon. 
 
 On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was 
unanimously voted:  To award bid package 1.2.1, Demolition & HAZMAT Removal, for the 
renovation of the Edgewood Pre-K Academy, to American Building Wreckers, in the amount of 
$1,673,371.00, and to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any necessary documents. 
 
 On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was 
unanimously voted:  To remove agenda item 16, which was placed on the agenda in error.  
  
13. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
 At 8:25 p.m., on motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member 
Rosengren, it was unanimously voted:  To enter into Executive Session to discussion the potential 
acquisition of 116 Marsh Road, Bristol, CT, Assessor's Map 64, Lot 1-1; Marsh Road, Bristol, CT, 
Assessor's Map 64, Lot 1; Marsh Road, Bristol, CT, Assessor's Map 61, Lot 16-1, and to take any 
action as necessary. 
 
 Discussion was held.  No votes were taken. 
 At 9:32 p.m., on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, 
it was unanimously voted:  To reconvene into Public Session. 
 
14. OTHER BUSINESS – None. 
  
15. ADJOURNMENT 
 
At 9:33 p.m., on motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member 
Rosengren, it was unanimously voted:  To adjourn.
